text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
The Governor of New South Wales Sir THOMAS BRISBANE, who gave his name to Queensland's capital, was born in 1773.
The man who invented the woolpress in Australia, CHRISTIAN KOERSTZ, was born in Denmark in 1847.
Australian featherweight boxing champion ALBERT "Griffo" GRIFFITHS, who killed one opponent in the ring, was born in 1871.
Australian artist JESSE HILDER, who died young of the artists' disease, tuberculosis, was born in 1881.
RAYMOND CHANDLER, U.S. novelist and creator of the Philip Marlowe detective character in "The Big Sleep" and "Farewell My Lovely" and many others, was born in 1888.
Australian actress CORAL BROWNE, who was married to actor VINCENT PRICE, was born in 1913.

Australian broadcaster and television compere, BERT NEWTON, was born in 1938 at North Fitzroy. He is the youngest of six children and began radio announcing at the age of 16. He moved to TV three years later.
English cricketer GRAHAM GOOCH was born in 1953.
Guitarist, synthesizer player and songwriter with Depeche Mode, MARTIN LEE GORE, was born in 1961. In 1989, his first solo album "Counterfeit" appeared.
British trumpet and keyboard player with 'Simply Red', TIM KELLET, was born in 1964.
** EVENTS **
1840 : The Union Act was passed by the British
Parliament, uniting Upper and Lower Canada with equal representation for both of the former provinces.
1858: The Oath of Allegiance in Britain was modified to
allow Jews to sit in Parliament.
1875 : ISAAC SINGER, U.S. inventor, died. He developed
the first practical sewing machine in 1851 which was the first to use continuous and curved stitching.
1885 : ULYSSES SIMPSON GRANT, commander of the Federal
army during the latter part of the U.S. Civil War and U.S. president from 1869-77, died.
1901: In Germany, Dr ROBERT KOCH advanced the theory that
rats could be carrying bubonic plague.
1904: Brisbane's first golf club was opened at suburban
Yeerongpilly.
1914: Freudian ideas came to prominence in the

international psychoanalytic community. The president of the International Association CARL GUSTAV JUNG resigned after SIGMUND FREUD distributed his paper of the "History of the Psychoanalysis Movement", which clearly outlined the differences between JUNG and FREUD. The major dispute in their teachings was over "libido". FREUD argued it signified sexual energy while JUNG said "libido" encompassed general mental energy. FREUDIAN theory prevailed.
1916: The Scottish chemist, Sir WILLIAM RAMSAY, who
discovered helium and isolated neon, xenon and krypton, died.
1929: A new era of broadcasting began in Australia with
the first transmission from the National Broadcasting Company from 3LO in Melbourne. There were 300,000 licensed radio sets in Australia, with an estimated audience of 120,000 people.
1930 : GLENN CURTISS, U.S. aviation pioneer whose
aircraft were widely used in World War One, died.
1940: Britain's auxiliary force was renamed the Home

Guard. The one-million-strong Local Defence Volunteers, which included many World War One veterans, was intended to protect Britain against an expected German invasion. The Home Guard was the subject of the long running television series "Dad's Army".
1948 : D. W. GRIFFITH, U.S. film producer and director of
the silent film epics "Birth of a Nation", and "Intolerance", died.
1951 : Marshal PHILIPPE PETAIN died in prison. He was
French army marshal and head of the collaborating Vichy government in France from 1940-44 and was subsequently sentenced to life in prison.
1952: In Egypt, General MOHAMMED NEGUIB seized power in a

military coup. King FAROUK subsequently fled the country. The coup followed a series of arms scandals in which FAROUK was accused on turning a blind eye to friends making massive profits, through supplying defective weapons to the army. There was rejoicing in the streets after FAROUK's departure on his
luxury yacht.
1954: The Chinese "accidentally" shot down a British
airliner.
1967: British cyclist TOMMY SIMPSON died from heat
exhaustion during the Tour de France.
1973 : EDWARD VERNON (EDDIE) RICKENBACKER, U.S. aviator
and ace fighter pilot during World War One, died.
1979: In Iran, AYATOLLAH KHOMEINI banned the broadcasting
of music, saying it corrupted youth.
1980: RUSS HINZE was named as Queensland's new police
minister. The man became known as the "Minister for Everything" because of the various portfolios he had administered.
1981: Three Australians, convicted of heroin trafficking
in Bangkok, were given sentences of between 20 and 33 years. It was one of Thailand's longest drug trials, involving former Sydney rugby league player PAUL HAYWARD, Sydney hairdresser
WARREN FELLOWS and Bangkok bar-owner, WILLIAM SINCLAIR. They were all arrested in 1978.
1982 : The International Whaling Commission voted for a
total ban on commercial whaling to take effect in 1985.
1986: Prince ANDREW married SARAH FERGUSON at
Westminister Abbey. They became the DUKE and DUCHESS OF YORK.
1989: American MARK CALCAVECCHIA won the British Golf
Open, defeating Australian's GREG NORMAN and WAYNE GRADY in a play-off.
1996 : JESSICA MITFORD, crusading author best known for
her indictment of the funeral industry in "The American Way of Death", died.
